description: MCP Secure deterministic policy ruleset v4. This file's SHA-256 is stored in every ScanRecord. v2 added AST severity scores, v3 combined the real Model B with AST corroboration. v4 expressed the same rules as declarative instances over contract findings (spec §7), keyed by registry slot, and adds the coverage rules: no PASS when a required analyzer did not run, when no code analyzer covered the source, or when no MCP tools were found. v5 (from adversarial testing) adds require_complete_source and require_resolved_descriptions, and counts a code analyzer that ran as coverage even when it found no function to score. v6 (Mid 1 review): a Model B fail-level finding inside a discovered MCP tool handler keeps its score without AST corroboration (tool arguments are attacker input by definition; the AST analyzer covers only Python, intra-procedural, and has no ssrf/sqli sinks, so v5 could not FAIL most real vulnerabilities),. sql_injection is excluded from that trust (database servers query by design). v7: the built-in TS/JS taint analyzer (ts_taint) corroborates Model B like the Python AST analyzer does, and its own findings need Model B to agree before they can FAIL.

rules.rationale: Fail-closed: if a required analyzer errored or is not configured, the server cannot PASS.
The corroboration caps and thresholds were tuned for a specific Model B; a different model must be re-released (release.py) before it can decide verdicts.
At least one code analyzer must actually analyse the source. Servers in languages no code analyzer supports (Go, Rust) or without source reach REVIEW, never PASS (decision D3).
If ingestion found no MCP tools, the analyzers could not tell tool input from internal code, and Model A had no descriptions to read.
A code file skipped for size or count limits is unanalysed code that will run. Padding a file past the limit must not be a way to PASS.
A tool description built at runtime (read from a file, concatenated from variables) is text an agent will see but Model A could not check.
Unsanitized tool input reaching a shell/exec sink within 2 hops is an immediate FAIL regardless of other analyzers.

Model B scores one function at a time and cannot see whether tool input reaches the risky call. A Model B finding keeps its score (and can FAIL) when a taint analyzer (Python ast_taint or TS/JS ts_taint) reports a medium/high flow of the same threat in an overlapping function of the same file, or (v6) when it lies inside a discovered tool handler with a raw score >= trusted_min_score: a tool handler receives attacker input by definition. Otherwise fail-level becomes 0.55 (REVIEW) and review-level 0.25 (evidence). sql_injection is excluded from tool-handler trust: database MCP servers run queries in their handlers by design (mongodb, redis, logfire scored 0.87-0.97 there), so it needs AST corroboration (Appendix E2). Threshold and exclusion chosen on eval run3gpu (148 scans): vulnerable FAIL 12/66 -> 21/66 with 0/23 benign FAIL.

The TS/JS taint analyzer is new and approximate (name-based call resolution). Its flows keep their score, and can FAIL, only when Model B flags the same threat in an overlapping function of the same file (two independent analyzers agree); alone a flow is REVIEW (high) or evidence (medium).
Highest effective finding score: >= fail threshold → FAIL, >= review threshold → REVIEW, else PASS.

analyzerPinsRationale: Artifact hashes the thresholds and caps of this ruleset were calibrated for. model_b_service/release.py updates the Model B pin when a new model is released. A slot reporting a different hash cannot PASS.
